description: The iter3/iter4 fix for FIND-001 (preserving external/confirmed/fill_tid) introduces a NEW, overly-broad allowlist pattern for fill_tid's string form that is never actually written by any real writer in this codebase, is never routed through either redaction layer (structured-field exemption, REQ-706), and would publish a secret-shaped alphanumeric string verbatim to the public branch if it were ever produced. `projectEarnField()`'s 'fill_tid' case (runtime/loop/ledger-publish.mjs:338-341) accepts either a finite number OR any string matching `SETTLEMENT_ID_VALUE = /^[A-Za-z0-9:_-]{1,128}$/` (ledger-publish.mjs:225). This is a materially wider charset/length envelope than 'a bounded identifier-shaped string' -- 128 chars of alphanumeric plus `:_-` is exactly the shape of many real-world API keys, session tokens, and bearer secrets (which typically avoid characters like spaces or `$` precisely because they are meant to survive URL/header encoding), and none of that is caught by redactBroaderSecretPatterns (which only matches base58 64-88 runs or 40+-hex runs -- an alphanumeric token using digits+letters in a non-base58, non-hex mix, e.g. containing both '0' and 'O'/'I'/'l', sails through untouched). The comment at ledger-publish.mjs:219-224 itself concedes this branch exists only 'in case a future writer serializes it as a string' -- it is dead code today: `skills/earn/hl-trade/lib/reconcile.py:144-148` (`tid = fill["tid"]`, built directly from Hyperliquid's userFills API, which the SAME file's own comment at ledger-publish.mjs:219-221 confirms is 'verified live as a JSON integer... never a string, in every real HL-sourced earn-ledger line') is the only real fill_tid writer in the repo, and it always writes a number. `skills/earn/lib/record.mjs` (the sole ledger-append entrypoint, called by reconcile.py's `record_line`) performs no field-level validation on fill_tid before `deriveLine`/`appendLedger` -- `assertOwnIdentityOnly` only checks for PII env vars, not field shape -- so there is no upstream guard preventing a future/buggy writer from putting an arbitrary token-shaped string into this field. Since the string branch bypasses BOTH redaction layers (the same exemption the 'sig'/'tx' structured fields get, correctly, because THEIR shapes are tightly bound to a real signature/hash format) while accepting a materially looser shape than either of those, this repeats the exact class of gap iter3's own adversary already ruled BLOCKING for `sig` (FIND-003, iteration-3), just for a currently-unreachable branch rather than an actively-populated one -- which lowers today's exploitability but does not change the structural correctness gap: REQ-702's own stated design principle ('structural parsing of a fixed machine format, never judgment', behavioral-spec.md:136) is violated by this specific sub-case, since a 128-char loose alphanumeric-with-punctuation string is not 'a fixed machine format'.

corroborating.note: `_build_payload`: `tid = fill["tid"]` passed straight into the ledger payload as `fill_tid` -- the ONLY real HL writer in this repo, and it is always the raw numeric value from Hyperliquid's userFills API, never a string.

`record()` calls `deriveLine(input)` then `assertOwnIdentityOnly(line)` (PII/identity check only) then `appendLedger` -- no field-shape validation of fill_tid anywhere in this pipeline, so nothing upstream would reject a string-typed fill_tid before it reaches the ledger file.

The only test covering the fill_tid string branch asserts a WELL-FORMED id (`hl-fill:12345`) round-trips and a value containing a space+`$` is dropped -- it does not assert that a plausible SECRET-shaped alphanumeric string (e.g. a 40-90 char API-key-like token using only [A-Za-z0-9_-]) is also rejected/redacted, so the test would keep passing even if this exact gap were exploited.
